name: Quicksand
label: Revelation
lede: Walter Schreifels left the youth crew behind, tuned down, and cut a seven-inch for Revelation that got a major label's attention. Two Polydor-era albums and two breakups later, Quicksand are on their fifth record.

eras.title: Tuned down, on Revelation
eras.text: Walter Schreifels had written the songs that defined Gorilla Biscuits and played bass in Youth of Today. With players from Bold, Beyond, Burn, Collapse and Absolution he built something slower, lower and louder, and Revelation put it out before the year was over.

years.h: Walter Schreifels starts a band, and the tunings drop
years.p: Schreifels sings and plays guitar, [[Tom Capone|88c3e80c-41b6-48c9-985c-26ad5d026abd]] takes lead guitar, [[Sergio Vega|a4256437-7cad-40b7-a135-9767863c90cf]] plays bass and [[Alan Cage|65d4abbb-054b-4106-a826-0cb2b306341e]] drums. [[Charlie Garriga|4f24f7e7-bc37-45d1-8f60-99bc992cd780]] of [[Outface|2fabef87-f53f-4792-b05b-6d54a8517d4c]] plays second guitar at the first shows, then drops out.

years.src: RevHQ Speak Up · Revelation Records catalog
years.h: A melted candle on the sleeve, Don Fury at the board
years.p: Four songs, cut in April 1990 at Don Fury's Demo Demo studio in New York, about six weeks after the band formed. [[Tim Singer|f59575a6-de2d-4eb3-9d6c-a076dcbcd603]] of Deadguy drew an alternate cover that went unused.
years.xp:
One listener's description, passed along by writer Anthony Pappalardo: 7 Seconds' New Wind crossed with [[Jane's Addiction|e3434cc7-d348-491a-9dc8-325af3d9086d]]. It was slower and more groove-driven than anything Schreifels had done in straight-edge hardcore, and kids who came for Gorilla Biscuits started tuning down in their own bands.

Within a year Quicksand went from opening slots to headlining rooms of nearly 2,000. Revelation's catalog (Rev 18) lists a first press of 5,000 black and 1,000 white vinyl, then yellow, blue, green and red repressings through 2015 and after.

years.h: The van dies an hour outside Buffalo
years.p: Quicksand's first tour, with Ray Cappo's [[Shelter|d5157104-76b1-4b8b-90c2-9ff994f940db]] and Zack de la Rocha's [[Inside Out|0049c4d7-6459-4b54-a865-fd19969f427f]], starts with the engine seizing on day one. Revelation's Jordan Cooper pays for the fix, and Quicksand miss their first set.
years.xp:
The van was the "Van of Suffering" that Beyond and Bold had used before them. The engine gave out about an hour outside Buffalo and took five days to replace, so the band rode in Shelter's bus while the van was towed.

The run left New York in June and went on to Cleveland, the Unisound in Reading and, at the end, City Gardens in New Jersey.

years.h: Boston's Channel puts Quicksand on top of the bill
years.p: About a year after the seven-inch, Quicksand headline a Boston room that held around 2,000.

eras.title: A major label for a seven-inch band
eras.text: Polydor signed a band with one seven-inch and a lot of word of mouth. Quicksand toured with everyone from Fugazi to White Zombie, made two major-label records, and split after a show in Hollywood.

yt: Dine Alone and Baphomet on the 1993 Rage tour
years.h: Polydor signs a band with one seven-inch
years.p: Per Wikipedia, Quicksand are the first post-hardcore band on a major. Tours follow behind [[Helmet|582fee78-d934-4603-9f5c-1729e0ca36b7]], [[Fugazi|233fc3f3-6de2-465c-985e-e721dbabbace]], [[Rage Against the Machine|3798b104-01cb-484c-a3b0-56adc6399b80]], [[Anthrax|b616d6f0-ec1f-4c69-8a79-12a97ece7372]] and [[White Zombie|cfe572bf-840f-4bed-934a-f69f4b1e90d4]], across North America and Europe.

years.big: "By the time we did Slip, that was our biggest influence."
years.h: Slip arrives on Polydor, with a cassette behind it
years.p: Walter Schreifels on the [[My Bloody Valentine|8ca01f46-53ac-4af2-8516-55a909c0905e]] tape the band picked up on an English tour. The album re-cuts Omission and Unfulfilled from the seven-inch, with Dine Alone as the single.
years.xp: Wikipedia counts about 250 shows behind Slip, and roughly 100,000 copies sold by 1995. The influences Quicksand have named run from [[Rites of Spring|b2ff1a6d-9198-4646-b068-8965242d245b]] and [[Embrace|9d1ad8e3-8740-429a-bdc5-52f96a9c4431]] to [[Public Enemy|bf2e15d0-4b77-469e-bfb4-f8414415baca]], [[Wire|7f2a8098-50e3-451c-8696-c5d9f64f4762]] and the [[Cocteau Twins|000fc734-b7e1-4a01-92d1-f544261b43f5]].

years.h: Back out with The Offspring
years.p: A US tour alongside [[The Offspring|23a03e33-a603-404e-bcbf-2c00159d7067]] runs into 1994, with the Freezing Process single.

years.h: Manic Compression charts at No. 135 on Island
years.p: Quicksand's second major-label album also reaches No. 9 on Heatseekers. Delusional hits No. 2 on the CMJ chart, and Revelation presses the vinyl edition.
years.xp:
Revelation's catalog (Rev 43) lists a test press of four copies and a first press of 3,008 black and 300 white vinyl.

The album also earned Quicksand a place on the first Vans Warped Tour.

years.h: Quicksand sign on for the first Warped Tour
years.p: The inaugural run of the traveling punk festival, with Manic Compression a few months old.

years.h: Quicksand end it in Hollywood, at their peak
years.p: After a show in Hollywood, Quicksand split at the height of their popularity. Wikipedia puts it down to fights inside the band and the grind of never getting off the road.

eras.title: Back together, briefly, and the album left in Stamford
eras.text: Two years off was enough to try again. They reconvened in Japan, recorded in Connecticut, toured with a rising Deftones, and then the old tensions came back and took a third album with them.

years.h: Osaka hosts the first Quicksand show since the split
years.p: The first Quicksand show since the 1995 split is in Osaka, Japan. A Hawaii date after it gets cancelled.

years.h: A Boulder show gets them a seat on the Deftones tour
years.p: Quicksand's first North American show in three years, in Boulder, leads to an invitation to stay on the road with Deftones and [[Snapcase|90f7f8df-db45-4a6c-89fb-9e912f77eabd]]. That tour starts November 3.

years.h: Six months in Stamford, and the album never comes out
years.p: In 1998 Quicksand spend six months recording new songs at Carriage House Studios with Steven Haigler. The old tensions return, the band stops in late 1999, and the record stays on the shelf.
years.xp:
The tour with Deftones had gone well enough that the band was asked to stay out longer. It wasn't enough to hold things together.

The unfinished material has circulated online ever since. Quicksand didn't play together again until 2012.

eras.title: The special guest in Pomona
eras.text: In the gap, Walter Schreifels made Rival Schools, Tom Capone played in Handsome and Instruction, Alan Cage joined Seaweed, and Sergio Vega became the bassist in Deftones. Revelation's 25th birthday got the four back on a stage, and five years later came a new album, Interiors, finished without Capone.

years.cap: Quicksand at Rock am Ring, Germany, June 2014, two years after the Pomona set
years.h: The "special guest" at Rev25 is Quicksand, all four of them
years.p: At Revelation's 25th anniversary shows at the Glass House in Pomona, the original line-up plays together for the first time in 13 years.
years.xp:
The five-song set ended with a cover of [[The Smiths|40f5d9e4-2de7-4f2d-ad41-e31a9a9fea27]]' How Soon Is Now? The label that had put out Quicksand's seven-inch 22 years earlier was throwing the party. By then Vega was the bassist in Deftones, the band that had taken Quicksand on tour in 1998.

A little over two months later they were at the Bowery Ballroom, and by January they were on a full North American tour.

years.cap: Walter Schreifels at Groezrock, Belgium, April 2013 (not a Quicksand set)
years.h: New York gets Quicksand back after 15 years
years.p: Bowery Ballroom, August 24, then Music Hall of Williamsburg the next night and FYF Fest in Los Angeles a week later.

years.cap: Quicksand at Rock am Ring, Germany, June 2014, a year after the tour
years.h: Quicksand go back on the road across North America
years.p: Their first North American tour in 15 years starts in January. In August they play Belgium's Pukkelpop festival.

years.h: Capone is arrested at a Phoenix CVS and leaves the tour
years.p: Hours before Quicksand's Crescent Ballroom show, [[Tom Capone|88c3e80c-41b6-48c9-985c-26ad5d026abd]] is arrested at a CVS on West Jefferson and charged with shoplifting and resisting arrest, per court documents Lambgoat obtained. The band says he's headed home.
years.xp:
The court documents, as MetalSucks relayed them, say Capone concealed 43 items in his backpack and pockets and walked past every register. An off-duty officer took his arm; Capone tried to break the grip and flee, and the arresting officer cut his elbow. He admitted to both charges.

The band's statement: "the road has proved to be a difficult environment for Tom who's headed home to work on his health." Quicksand finished the tour as a trio, Schreifels covering all the guitar. Capone never rejoined.

years.h: Interiors ends a 22-year wait on Epitaph
years.p: Announced in August with Illuminant, their first new song in 22 years. The album reaches No. 1 on Billboard's Heatseekers chart, No. 9 on Alternative Albums and No. 142 on the Billboard 200.

eras.title: Three people, still loud
eras.text: As a three-piece, Quicksand made records faster than they ever had in the nineties. Stephen Brodsky of Cave In filled out the stage for a while, and a new label brought a fifth album in the summer of 2026.

years.h: Triptych Continuum is the first record without Capone
years.p: A 12" EP on Epitaph for Record Store Day, with Schreifels playing both rhythm and lead guitar.

yt: Dine Alone, live on KEXP, with Brodsky
years.h: Distant Populations brings in Cave In's Stephen Brodsky
years.p: [[Stephen Brodsky|a0ff602c-7f3e-472d-8786-953da6cd7591]] guests on Colossus, then joins Quicksand's live band as touring guitarist, making them a four-piece on stage through 2023.
years.xp: The singles came first: Inversion on April 13 and Missile Command on June 23. The album went out digitally August 13, with vinyl following September 25.

yt: Slip at 30, the Iodine event at Generation Records
years.h: Slip turns 30 with a 64-page book
years.p: Boston's Iodine Recordings reissues Slip from the original 1993 masters, with a hardcover of photos and posters and a foreword from Schreifels.
years.xp:
The expanded edition adds a bonus track, the same Smiths cover from the Rev25 set, How Soon Is Now?, and a run of limited vinyl variants.

The booklet collects tributes from [[Scott Ian|40b0dfb0-d7e7-4a92-b0fa-12ed9af54993]], Thursday's [[Geoff Rickly|132f1d42-4567-4dca-b6e1-3765726f91dc]], Refused's [[Dennis Lyxzén|d7bb37a5-3d48-4a2f-a761-fe66d5cdb409]] and Rise Against's [[Tim McIlrath|157e6a4c-5233-42f8-83f5-e43b0c04641a]].

years.h: Hot Water Music and Quicksand share a record
years.p: The split comes out through Equal Vision, the label that will release Quicksand's next album.

years.h: Bring On the Psychics arrives on Equal Vision
years.p: Quicksand's fifth album, announced in April with their new Equal Vision deal. Stereogum names it Album of the Week.
years.xp: Tom Breihan's Stereogum review, published July 14, hears "a galloping tempo, a clean vocal, a big riff with a whole lot of bounce."
